question: Which layer owns specialization (version identity, context keys, budgets, traversal) — and can the residualization stack's three independent traversals become one? Ranked above: whether abc-opt residue should be function-wide or per-version, and whether the portable-C sink survives.
evidence: .ralphi/optimizer-residual-redesign/experiments/1-rederive.md (derivation from CONTRACT, ownership audit with citations, projections, measurement plan)

REFACTOR.md:811 — documented version-budget divergence (10 versions at one PC vs approved 8 per original PC) as the consequence of policy having no single owner

No timings run; all costs are labelled structural projections with a fixture-based measurement plan
decision: Adopt the candidate in ARCHITECTURE.md: five concepts with one owner each — module facts (leaders, call graph, SCC/recursion, unknown calls), symbolic machine, context key policy, version (pc,key,owning residual function), binding. One sink-agnostic driver owns traversal, join materialization, queue order and the canonical-generic fallback; sinks own only residue (native: none; C: per-version residual.asdl block; ABC: per-version bytecode + locally scheduled DAG). Q4 and Q5 are answered yes on evidence (fold module facts and key policy into the core; no policy content, pure duplication). Named deletion set recorded: abc-opt call-graph copy + ArgumentFact fixpoint + path-tree walk, residual_analysis.c as a separate owner, symbolic.c DFS helpers, and the private drivers/leader discovery/key canonicalization in residualize.c and residual_builder.c. Q1 (abc-opt adopting block versions) is surfaced as a version-policy hard gate rather than decided; Q2 (which version-budget policy is authoritative) and Q3 (portable-C scope) are also open.
next: Settle Q1 with evidence: measure interpreter dispatch and optimized-module size on the existing optimizer fixture corpus for shared (versioned) ABC blocks versus the duplicated path tree, and confirm the ABC encoding/verifier permits multiple versions of a non-entry block. Also verify the claim that per-version residue can keep abc-opt's motivating canonicalization (CGET.A 0; MULC.A 0; CGET.B 1; MULC.B 1; ADD.A; RET) without a function-wide DAG, and that idempotence/byte-determinism hold under the versioned sink. question: Under a versioned ABC sink, is residue a function-wide value DAG (versions select only control) or per-version residue whose cross-edge values are constants plus the binding's locations — and what must a version key contain? Enabling facts tested in the same probe: is a versioned non-entry block representable/verifiable, and what does the incumbent path tree actually cost?
evidence: experiments/2-abc-probe.lua — new fixtures assembled with the repo assembler, optimized through abc_optimize_mapped (frontend/let/optimize.lua), decoded, and executed in interpreted + jit=threaded modes; reproducible

experiments/2-abc-versioned-sink.md §1–2 — measured table and disassembly: 88-instruction 12-branch function → 16,382 instructions (186×, one input RET copied 4,096×, ~24 ms); 13 branches → whole function retained after ~22 ms exploration; branch+store, branch+trap, store+branch all retained unoptimized; multi-result join 8 → 19 instructions; all cases idempotent and execution-identical; documented canonical fixture (docs/abc-opt.md:82-91) emitted exactly as CGET0_A; MULC_A 0; CGET1_B; MULC_B 1; ADD_A; RET_A 2 1

src/optimize.c:157 and :747 — a branching function refuses any non-call effect node, regardless of effect position (the measured coverage cliff); :361-387 simulate_tree DFS; :705-723 emit_phi_tree/PhiPatches; :153-161 linear hash-consing; :791-808 N:1 provenance

src/residual_builder.c:851-877, 996-1062, 1083-1123 — the portable-C sink already implements the target policy: canonicalize non-constants to homes, keep constants in edge keys, forget them at loop entries, widen recursive keys, all-home fallback at the budget, one block argument per key slot
src/symbolic.c:33-38 (key equality compares sink-owned reg) vs :62-75 (canonical generic form hardcodes HOME(s,i), which the ABC sink cannot consume — optimize.c:165-170 rejects HOME)
src/verify.c:131-134 — CALL/TCALL must target a function entry, so an entry is a single widened version (the round-1 'delete ArgumentFact' item was wrong as stated); :266-267 RET contract

Measured representability: the incumbent path tree already emits duplicate non-entry blocks (max input-pc multiplicity 2/3/16/…/4096) accepted by the verifier and all execution modes; only a second function entry is forbidden
decision: Adopt per-version residue for ABC and make the version key = constants + binding-defined locations, never sink residue identity. This corrects ARCHITECTURE.md: the C sink's canonicalize/version_for policy is the single shared key rule (core owns equality/family/budget/recursion widening/entry widening); the binding supplies its location vocabulary and canonical generic form (ABC's stable location is a C-frame slot written by the join, read by the target body). Function-wide ABC value graph with node ids in keys is rejected (needs dominance-safe cross-version home reuse, keeps O(n²) hash-consing and path-use counting, and the measured blow-up is control duplication). Q6 and Q7 are answered; Q5 is refined to 'yes for the rule, binding for locations'. Q1 is now an explicit recommendation to the user, not an unknown: adopt versioned blocks for abc-opt (measured exponential growth, 4096-path whole-function cliff, and blanket refusal of branch-plus-effect functions; representability already demonstrated), still surfaced as the version-policy hard gate because output bytes and analysis policy change. The round-1 deletion set is corrected: the entry-fact lattice and single-entry-version rule are required, not duplication.

Also settle Q2 (budget authority: 8 total per original PC vs the implemented 10) because the shared driver now needs one budget number for ABC too.
